newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Western Metals readies new zinc mine.
newsitem.headline: Western Metals readies new zinc mine.

text.p: Zinc and lead miner Western Metals Ltd said on Tuesday its Kapok mine in Western Australia was gearing up for production after the nearby Cadjebut mine ceased operating around the end of the year.
"We've taken the pressure off producing from Kapok because the Cadjebut mine is still kicking on," Burt Lambert, development manager for Western Metals, told Reuters from Perth.
The Kapok lode was initially designed to take over from Cadjebut, which is nearing the end of its projected mine life, supplying ore to a processing mill at the Cadjebut site.
Eventually, Kapok would produce a maximum 600,000 tonnes of ore a year, Lambert said.
Western Metals also mines the Goongewa deposit and is developing the Blendevale mine, which it expects to commission in mid-1998.
Western Metals has said it hopes to be producing about 160,000 tonnes of zinc and 60,000 tonnes of lead in concentrates a year by 1999, making it the world's seventh biggest zinc company.
